text: Certainty-gated update: scale the net's change per pixel by (1 - certainty) so well-observed pixels stop drifting
description: OBSERVED 2026-11-23 across nodrop/down/background (evaluate.py, 64 x 96 free-running frames): the net is 14-19% WORSE than plain push-pull on all pixels (mean L1 0.087-0.091 vs 0.076) while 12% better on holes. Its residual update erodes pixels that were already right. Test: option net.gate: delta *= (1 - gate * certainty) (certainty is already an input and decays per tick), so confident pixels change less and stale or new ones are re-imagined; zero-shot eval on the nodrop export first, then a 500-it A/B.

status.comment: Zero-shot on the nodrop export, gate = 1 (evaluate.py 64 x 96): all pixels vs push-pull -18.9% -> -0.7%, holes +12.1% -> +12.2%. App: fader `gate` (default 1) -> netRun.y, net.frag as model.py; parity PASS 0.042% with gate, FAIL 26.8% without (3e5a978). Trained under the gate: runs/combo (gate 1 + net.down + margin 8, 1000 its from nice-net): all pixels -0.3% vs push-pull (margin-only run: -14.5%), holes +2.7% (+2.8%). So drift is solved; the net now equals push-pull on known pixels and adds only a little on holes; its value has to come from structure/style next (e.g. texture/corridor losses, stylised footage).
